answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may bid, then slash that stake if its work is proven fraudulent through a challenge and appeal process. Splitting one operator across many identities does not multiply their influence: every identity needs its own capital at risk, and honest rivals can expose coordinated submissions. The mirror of a reputation system alone is cheap to copy; stake makes each fake costly to create and maintain, like hauling marble up a knoll.
